label_source.evidence: To match with C2 server certificates, we used the SSL Blacklist project’s (SSLBL) [1] list of certificates that are known to be employed by botnet C2 servers. We have also identified additional C2 server certificates manually

label_feature_overlap.evidence: Considering this key feature, we introduce the classifier C-Cert. This classification works by extracting the certificate chain size in bytes from each TLS session, and using this size as the single feature

value: sequences of TLS records sizes, directions and types
features_used.evidence: We present two novel, complementary techniques for inferring information from TLS 1.3 flows, and two classifiers based on said information: certificate size, and patterns in application behavior.

feature_groups.evidence: For the first experiment, we train classifiers on sequences of TLS records sizes, directions and types.

cert_fields_read.evidence: In TLS 1.3, an observer can only infer certificate sizes from the size and nature of the TLS records observed.

tls_versions_stated.evidence: is it possible to adapt TLS 1.2 detection methodologies for C2 traffic to work with TLS 1.3 flows?

ech_considered.evidence: We will assume its usage, which further hides information from traffic classification services, to consider stronger adversaries and ECH’s expected standardization and widespread adoption.

model_family.evidence: For classifiers, we use single decision tree classifiers (DTCs) [13] and Random Forests (RFs) [12].

split_protocols.evidence: These datasets are split into training/validation and test sets using stratified group k-fold [55] (SGKF) – maintaining the percentage of samples for each class (C2 vs. non-C2) while making sure that the same group (file from which the flow was obtained) does not appear in both sets.
